LPC supervision and trauma therapy in Austin, Texas

Reem Glasco, LPC-S, is a Licensed Professional Counselor Supervisor in Austin, Texas. She has held Texas supervisor status since 2009 and is an EMDRIA Approved Consultant, a NARM therapist and a Somatic Experiencing Practitioner. She sees adults and young adults for developmental trauma, C-PTSD, anxiety, panic and depression, and supervises LPC Associates across the state. Her clinical center is IFS-informed EMDR: processing that consults the protective parts of a person instead of overriding them, with Somatic Experiencing setting the pace and NARM tracking the patterns underneath. It is the same lens whether you are a supervisee or a client. Supervision and EMDR consultation run online statewide, and some of the work happens on a trail or with horses rather than on a screen.

The four ways Reem works with therapists

Supervision, consultation, ethics hours and retreats are different things, and most therapists arrive wanting one of them in particular. All of it runs online across Texas, apart from the parts that deliberately happen on a trail or with horses.

LPC supervision

Your 3,000 hours, supervised online anywhere in Texas. Four hours a month, trauma-informed, with EMDR consultation included while you are here. If you are an associate working toward licensure, start here.

EMDR consultation

Hours toward certification with an EMDRIA Approved Consultant. Online, focused on IFS-informed EMDR for phases one and two.

Ethics CEUs

The six ethics hours Texas asks for each renewal period, on secondary trauma. One online, or two in person on a trail walk among horses.

Retreats and training

Mindful trail retreats and equine-assisted training for Texas therapists. For when the growth edge is yours rather than a client's.

Four ways Reem works with clients

Reem sees a small number of adults and young adults for developmental trauma, C-PTSD, anxiety, panic and depression. When her schedule is full, the practice's LPC Associates have openings, including at sliding-scale fees.

IFS-informed EMDR

Internal agreement from the protective parts first, then processing.

Helps when EMDR has been tried before and stalled, or part of you wants this and part of you really does not.

Somatic Experiencing

The pace your nervous system can actually hold, built rather than tested.

Helps when anxiety lives in your chest and stomach more than in your thoughts, or talking about it has stopped helping.

NARM

The pattern underneath, and where it was learned.

Helps when the trouble is a lifelong pattern rather than one event, and understanding your history has not changed it.

Equine-assisted therapy

What the body does around a horse that notices everything.

Helps when you talk more easily with something else going on, or you are working on boundaries. Adults only.

These four interlock rather than alternate, and the room is optional: walk and talk therapy happens on a trail in central Texas, and equine sessions run with the horses near Dripping Springs. Learn more about therapy at Finding Balance, including fees, formats, who each path suits and what a first session looks like.

Something to try before we ever meet

Longer out-breaths than in-breaths tell a nervous system it is allowed to stand down. One minute is enough to feel the difference, which is also the argument for teaching it to clients before you teach them anything else.

If the circle distracts you, ignore it and count: in for four, hold for two, out for six.

one minute

In for four, hold for two, out for six.

Effort-less Self-Care: 7 Easy Steps to Calm and Connection

Breath is one of the seven. The others are the same size: find a comfortable space, face the light, feel the body, name the emotion, ground through the senses. Each step pairs a watercolor with room to write beside it, so the workbook and the journal are one volume. Nothing in it needs fixing, and none of it takes long.
